subject.title: [Refactor] Consolidate synthetic log formats across MCP service pipelines

question: Should core OpenClaw tools and Codex supervision expose one stable fatal-diagnostic contract, or may each owner keep its own startup prefix?
rationale: Source ownership is intentionally split between core MCP code and a plugin-owned Codex entrypoint, while the issue provides no consumer or compatibility contract that makes identical output necessary.

options.title: Keep owner-specific diagnostics
options.body: Retain the existing ownership split and close this cleanup unless a concrete parser or operator workflow requires identical output.

options.title: Add a structured shared seam
options.body: Define a minimal public helper or diagnostic record at the supported core/plugin boundary and cover both entrypoints with contract tests.

options.title: Align wording independently
options.body: Use equivalent human-facing wording in each owner without introducing a cross-boundary shared module.

recommendation.title: Keep owner-specific diagnostics
recommendation.body: Retain the existing ownership split and close this cleanup unless a concrete parser or operator workflow requires identical output.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work connects this person most directly to both Codex runtime behavior and MCP integration decisions.
